`ds` has `time` and `time_relative` as coordinates.
`ds.set_xindex("time_relative")` makes `time_relative` the index for dimension `time`.
Wait, `ds` has `time` as a dimension.
`ds = xr.Dataset(data_vars={"signal": xr.DataArray(np.zeros((3, 2)), dims=("time", "position"), coords={"time": [12, 13, 14]})})`
`ds.time` is a coordinate and also the dimension name.
`ds = ds.assign_coords(time_relative=(ds.time - 12))`
`ds = ds.set_xindex("time_relative")`

Now `ds.signal` has dimension `time` and coordinates `time` and `time_relative`.
`da` has dimension `position` and no coordinates.

When doing `ds.signal - da`, they are aligned.
`ds.signal` has an index on `time`.
`da` does not have a `time` dimension.

The `Aligner` (which is what `self` is in `assert_no_index_conflict`) is created during `align(self, other)`.
